caption: The drawing features a large, ornate, scalloped-edge silver tray with intricate floral and leaf patterns decorating its rim. In the center of the tray is a detailed coat of arms, which includes a shield divided into quadrants, with two barrels on the left and right and two windmill sails crossed in saltire in the upper and lower sections. Flanking the shield, there is a male figure in colonial attire holding a staff on the left and a Native American male figure holding a bow on the right. Above the shield is a crown with floral scrollwork. A banner below the shield reads "SIGILLUS CIVITAT: NOV: EBORAC," and beneath the banner is an assortment of objects such as barrels, a caduceus, a cornstalk, a beaver, and other items arranged in a decorative manner. The rim of the tray also features a dense, symmetrical arrangement of leafy and floral patterns. Below the main image is a side profile view of the tray, showing three ornate, clawed feet and a beaded edge. The entire composition is rendered in precise black and white linework on a beige background, with the artist's signature "Clayton Braun" visible in the lower right corner.
title: Silver Salver
